title: Extended verdict-landscape raster — 17 cells H_312..H_330 (DYN vs STRUCT SUPP-rate, H_326 5× pattern recheck)
question: Does H_326's finding (DYN supp-rate ≥ 2× STRUCT supp-rate) hold after extending the raster from 10 to 17 cells?
engine: pure hexa-lang tabulation of (cell, kernel_class, verdict_tier); kernel_class declared from each cell's method (timestep=DYN · static Phi=STRUCT · struct+dyn-gate=HYBRID · raster=META) INDEPENDENT of verdict_tier

falsifier_eval.F331_1_RATIO_GE_2x_COND: FAIL — 1.71× < 2.0 (H_326's earlier 5× has degraded with extension)
falsifier_eval.F331_2_RATIO_GE_2x_STRICT: PASS — 2.57× > 2.0 (the direction holds when we count strict 🟢 only)

verdict_derived: 🟢 SUPPORTED-CONDITIONAL — H_326's qualitative direction (DYN > STRUCT supp-rate) survives extension, but the magnitude degrades sharply (5× → 1.71-2.57×). The cause is the new DYN cells H_327/H_329/H_330 all returning 🔴, exposing that DYN-kernel is necessary but not sufficient: scale-trivial dynamics (n=4 ECA fixed-point dominated, descriptor-orthogonal) still falsify. The honest extended finding: DYN > STRUCT by factor ~2 at strict-supp count, with the qualitative ordering robust but the 5× magnitude an artifact of the smaller 10-cell sample.
verdict: 🟢 SUPPORTED-CONDITIONAL (qualitative direction holds; magnitude degrades H_326 5× → 2.57× strict / 1.71× cond)

comparison_to_H_326.degradation: 5× → 2.5× (strict) — H_326 over-estimated DYN dominance due to small sample

honest_limits: Class labels are author-assigned (post-hoc from method); a blind labeling would harden the claim
Cond-supp counts 🟢-conditional as positive; binary strict-supp is more conservative — choose based on use-case
